evidence: RUNTIME HALF (fact list vs test.sh launch at test.sh:97-111 and the generated app-restart.sh): (1) entry path and start command: instruction.md:15 'Put the application in /app ... It must start with node /app/server.js'; integration.md:5. (2) port: instruction.md:15 'listen on port 3000 (honour PORT if it's set)'; integration.md:5-6 adds 0.0.0.0; test.sh sets PORT=3000 and probes 127.0.0.1:3000; app_context URL http://localhost:3000 (local only, lesson 13 ok). (3) storage/DB_PATH: instruction.md:15 'keep its durable data in /app/app.db, honouring DB_PATH when that is set'; integration.md:7-8; test.sh passes DB_PATH=$APP_DB (/app/app.db or /tmp/submission/app.db). (4) health path: instruction.md:15 'expose GET /api/health as a check that never touches the database'; integration.md:9-10; test.sh probe_ready (line 48) uses /api/health with / as fallback. (5) fixed clock: none injected by test.sh or task.toml and no criterion depends on absolute time; only relative 15 s windows, stated at instruction.md:5 and hireops_rules.md section 5. N-A item. (6) seed: instruction.md:15,17 '/assets/seed_data.json', 'Copy what you need into /app; /assets and /instructions are unavailable at runtime', 'Load ... once, start with no shipped database, and keep new work across restarts'; hireops_rules.md section 9 explains read markers, candidate wording and page size in the file. Seed facts the judge relies on are derivable: Platform Engineer Applied Greta Lindqvist/Ade Bello/Marco Rossi and Screen Priya Nair/Samuel Ortiz by position, Noor's note text, 120 messages on APP-101, Lena APP-301 with 3 messages and read_count 2 giving 1 unread. (7) accounts: instruction.md:19 password Hireops!2026 with all 10 emails and roles; seed users carry the display names used by app_context. (8) Launch conditions beyond the row list are also stated: uid 65534, possible writable copy, cwd not /app, env -i with only PATH/HOME/NODE_PATH/PORT/DB_PATH (hireops_rules.md section 8 vs test.sh:104-111); NODE_PATH packages, no installs (instruction.md:15, integration.md:3-4 vs Dockerfile global express/better-sqlite3); symlink policy (integration.md:16-19 vs test.sh:72-83); one process serving UI and API (instruction.md:15); restart durability for restart_app (instruction.md:17, integration.md:8-9). Network is public (task.toml network_mode public), so no offline constraint is needed; instruction.md:15 states the server must not depend on outside data services while the browser may use a CDN. GRADED-DEMANDS HALF: walked all 38 functional, 5 polish and 5 visual criteria plus both gates against instruction.md and hireops_rules.md. Each has a public sentence: job fields and places as a whole number 1-50 and manager from hiring-manager accounts (rules 2); add candidate at bottom of Applied, email validity, case-insensitive per-job duplicate, error at the field keeping typed values, candidate-account email links the application (rules 2); one-stage moves, no skips, reject needs a reason, Hired not rejectable, reopen only to rejected-from stage and clears reason (rules 3 Moving a card); arrival at bottom and shared persisted manual order (Order inside a stage); interview places, reorder in a full Interview, freed place usable at once (Interview places); manager late stages on own jobs only, observer/candidate never move (Who may move what); 409 stale move naming who (Two people at once; instruction.md:3); optimistic move put back with reason and focus on the card's controls (Shown at once); multi-card board-order arrival, all-or-none, places counted for the set (Moving several together); undo restores stage, place and reason, blocked by any move/reorder/reject/reopen of those cards or overfill, notes do not count, once only, superseded by a later move (Undo); note permissions and per-browser note draft (Internal notes); Activity lines with reason, newest first, job filter, no line for refusals (rules 4); 15 s live updates preserving typing, focus, open card/conversation and scroll (rules 5; instruction.md:5); plain text, line breaks, Enter/Shift+Enter, empty focused box, failed send kept and explained (Messages); latest 30 oldest first scrolled to newest, earlier 30 at a time, remaining count, anchor kept (Long conversations); per-person unread, total, scrolled-up notice (Unread); seen semantics incl. hiring manager and observer exclusion (Seen); per-conversation drafts surviving navigation, reload and session end, sign-in prompt at latest on the next server action, invisible to other users (Drafts; instruction.md:7); candidate list with title, team and wording table, privacy, staff actions refused (rules 7); 401/403/404 statuses (rules 1). Visual rows grade desktop craft only, consistent with instruction.md:11 ('A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'). Lessons file checked for this row: lessons 1/12 (graded demand without a brief sentence) none found; lesson 13 (public address in judge prompts) only localhost; lesson 8 (modifier-click) handled in app_context.md lines on holding the key. Counterexamples tried: (a) broken-but-passing: an app hard-coding port 3000 and ignoring PORT still runs because test.sh sets PORT=3000, and an app ignoring DB_PATH writes /app/app.db, which test.sh makes writable via chown 65534; both are harmless for grading and the contract is still stated. (b) conforming alternative that fails: an app resolving seed/UI from cwd, reading /assets at runtime, needing an extra env var, installing packages, symlinking globals, or touching the DB in /api/health; each is warned against in the brief or notes, so such a failure is the builder's, not a hidden contract.
notes: Note (P3, not a defect): hro_job_open refuses a blank title; hireops_rules.md section 2 says 'A job has a title' rather than stating a title is required. A natural reading covers it.

Note (P3): hro_thread_access expects Noor's send replay on another application's conversation to be refused 'as not found'; the 404 rule in hireops_rules.md section 1 is phrased for 'an application that isn't theirs'. Each application has exactly one conversation (section 6), so the reading is reasonable.

Note (P3): hro_pol_session_resume and the draft-isolation legs need a sign-out control; the brief implies it ('get signed out', 'nobody else who signs in on that browser') and the skill treats identity surfaces as house convention.

Note: instruction.md:17 says /assets is unavailable at runtime while task.toml artifacts include /assets and test.sh chmods it; the brief is stricter than the verifier, which cannot make a conforming app fail.
